title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon, former SNL cast member, is performing in Boston and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, this week.
Nealon's comedic work now includes tweets, a YouTube show 'Hiking with Kevin', and a new stand-up special 'Loose in the Crotch'.
Raised in Connecticut, Nealon previously worked at a Dunkin' Donuts in Bridgeport before becoming a comedian.

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras hit by a 95 MPH fastball from Dodgers pitcher Will Klein.
Contreras stayed in the game briefly but was replaced defensively in the next half-inning.
Contreras leads Red Sox in multiple offensive categories, including batting average and home runs.

title: After Patriots coaching stint, DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech staff
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: DeAndre Hopkins joins Georgia Tech as assistant wide receivers coach after Patriots training camp coaching stint.
Hopkins praised for his leadership and offensive knowledge, strengthens ties with Georgia Tech's offense coordinator, George Godsey.
Hopkins remains noncommittal about retiring from playing NFL, focusing on new coaching position.

title: Could Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both make the Patriots 53-man roster?
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Patriots wide receiver Efton Chism is vying for a position on the 53-man roster amid fierce competition.
Kyle Williams, initially considered seventh in line, has improved significantly in training camp and is a strong contender.
The Patriots' receiver room faces tough decisions, with seven contenders for potentially only six roster spots for Week 1.

title: Reports: OF George Springer interested in trade to Red Sox, team eyeing INF Xavier Edwards
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: George Springer, currently with the Blue Jays, is open to a trade to the Boston Red Sox.
The Red Sox are interested in Miami Marlins infielder Xavier Edwards to strengthen their infield.
Springer is batting .234 this season, while Edwards, a base-stealer, has a .292 average and is arbitration-eligible in 2027.

title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' featuring Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway is now streaming on Hulu.
'The Drama,' a dark comedy with Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, is available on HBO Max.
Season 1 of 'Furious,' starring Emmy Rossum, is streaming on Hulu.

title: Here’s how home, away broadcasts reacted to Jarren Duran’s on-field flare-up
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Jarren Duran went viral for expressing frustration over a play during the Red Sox's win against the Athletics.
NESN and WEEI broadcasters criticized Duran's public outburst, questioning its appropriateness during the game.
Red Sox may trade Duran ahead of the deadline, with interest affected by his recent on-field actions.

title: Drake Maye on building chemistry with A.J. Brown: ‘I am not going to shy away from him.’
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown are building chemistry during New England Patriots training camp, evident in recent practice performances.
Maye connected with Brown during drills, including a precise end zone throw, enhancing their on-field connection.
Maye remains committed to involving Brown in plays, aiming to improve team dynamics through consistent communication and practice.

title: Drake Maye, A.J. Brown heat up and other takeaways from Day 6 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye completes 18-of-19 throws in team drills as he builds rapport with A.J. Brown at Patriots training camp.
Romeo Doubs makes notable play with a fade ball touchdown, showcasing his role in the Patriots' revamped offense.
Veterans Carlton Davis III and Christian Barmore absent from Friday's practice; Barmore managing workload and health.

title: Massachusetts falls out of top 10 in best state rankings by U.S. News & World Report
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts dropped to 11th in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best States rankings, down from 9th last year.
The state maintained second place in healthcare but ranked poorly in fiscal stability (39th) and infrastructure (38th).
Utah, South Dakota, and Minnesota took the top three spots; New Hampshire fell to sixth from second place.
